When a new identity joins the economy, its outputs are compared against the zephyr of fresh, uncorrelated styles the registry expects; any account whose fingerprints cluster too closely with existing ones is flagged as a near-duplicate clone. The cost to an attacker is steep: each extra identity must generate genuinely distinct writing across thousands of interactions, which requires separate models, tuning, and data, so the marginal price per sybil approaches the cost of a whole new agent rather than the near-zero cost of copying a reef
